name: A Heart That Seeks
focus: Begin by turning your attention toward God. You do not have to perform; you only have to come.
prompt: Lord, You are the one I am looking for.
points: Thank God for His promise that He can be found.
Name the things that have been competing for your attention.
Ask for a fresh hunger for His presence, not only His gifts.
Sit in silence for two minutes and let your heart rest in Him.

name: The Kingdom First
focus: Pray for God's rule to come into the ordinary places of your life — your home, your work, your city.
prompt: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, here in me.
points: Ask God to search your heart for any area where you have taken the throne.
Pray for His will to be done in your family and closest relationships.
Pray for your city: for justice, peace, and the courage to serve.
Ask for eyes to see the kingdom opportunities already around you.

name: Daily Bread
focus: Bring your needs honestly. Provision is not a reward for worry; it is a gift from a Father who knows.
prompt: Father, give me what I need for today, and trust You for tomorrow.
points: Thank God for one specific provision from this week.
Name the need you are tempted to carry alone.
Ask for wisdom to work, save, and share what He gives.
Pray for someone in your circle who is in need right now.

name: Under the Shadow
focus: You are not praying for a life without danger. You are praying for the presence of God inside it.
prompt: You are my refuge and my fortress, and I trust You.
points: Name the fear that has been loudest this week.
Ask God to be your dwelling place, not only your emergency exit.
Pray protection over your home, your work, and your travels.
Pray for courage to walk forward in faith, not paralysis.

name: A House of Peace
focus: Pray over the people you live with and the home you are building, one small act of love at a time.
prompt: Father, let Your love be the walls of our home.
points: Thank God for the people in your home, even the difficult ones.
Name one relationship that needs patience or repair.
Ask for words that build rather than words that wound.
Pray that your home would become a place of welcome and safety.

name: Wisdom to Lead
focus: Leadership is stewardship. Pray for wisdom to carry people, not merely to manage tasks.
prompt: Give me a heart that serves and wisdom that builds.
points: Pray for the leaders in your life, especially those you find difficult.
Ask God to show you the people He has entrusted to your care.
Name one decision that needs wisdom; ask for clarity.
Pray for humility to receive correction and courage to make the call.

name: Through the Storm
focus: Bring the storm to Jesus. He is not distant from your fear, and He is not silent in your night.
prompt: Be still, and know that You are God.
points: Tell God exactly what you are feeling, without editing.
Ask Him to speak peace to the part of you that is panicking.
Pray for strength to do the next right thing, not the whole future.
Ask for people around you who can carry hope while you are tired.

name: A Grateful Heart
focus: Gratitude is not denial. It is choosing to see what is still good, even in a hard season.
prompt: Thank You, Lord, for who You are and for what You have done.
points: Name three gifts from the last twenty-four hours.
Thank God for one thing you have been taking for granted.
Ask Him to heal the places where bitterness has taken root.
Pray for a heart that is generous with thanks and slow to complain.

name: Forgive and Be Free
focus: Forgiveness is not pretending the wound did not happen. It is releasing the debt to God.
prompt: Lord, have mercy on me, and make me merciful.
points: Ask God to reveal anything you need to confess; receive His forgiveness.
Name the person you are holding to a debt; ask for grace to release them.
Pray for the person who hurt you, even if you do not feel like it.
Ask God to heal the wound, not just remove the anger.

name: Healing and Strength
focus: Pray for healing of body, mind, and spirit, and for strength to keep walking while you wait.
prompt: Lord, heal what only You can heal.
points: Name the area where you need healing, and ask boldly.
Pray for the doctors, caregivers, and friends who are helping.
Ask for strength to do the next faithful thing while you wait.
Pray for someone else who is sick or discouraged today.
